objective.value: Determine the genome-wide fitness effect of each Escherichia coli gene under sub-lethal gentamicin exposure using a high-resolution CRISPRi screening library, compare fitness changes with anaerobic conditions (under which gentamicin is ineffective), and identify regulatory mechanisms of gentamicin defense, including the role of the two-component response regulator CpxR.
objective.notes: Objective stated in Abstract and Introduction; no engineering/production objective is reported.

hypothesis.value: Implicit, not explicitly stated: genome-wide CRISPRi fitness profiling of E. coli under gentamicin, contrasted with anaerobic conditions where gentamicin fails to enter cells, will reveal genes and regulators whose knockdown alters gentamicin sensitivity via respiration and membrane potential.
hypothesis.notes: The paper states aims and rationale but no formal hypothesis; value is a bounded inference from the Introduction.

inference.rationale: Introduction states that gentamicin is ineffective anaerobically because it fails to enter E. coli without oxygen, that understanding this may shed light on resistance mechanisms, and that the authors therefore examined fitness changes under gentamicin and anaerobic conditions using a high-resolution CRISPRi library; the implicit hypothesis is reconstructed only from these explicit statements.

Enrichment ratio (ER): per-sgRNA ratio of abundance with dCas9 co-expression vs initial pool; per-gene ER = median of normalized sgRNA ratios across targeted positions; ER<1 detrimental, ER=1 neutral, ER>1 beneficial
Pearson correlation coefficient (r = 0.93 between gentamicin and anaerobic ER ratios) and PCA on ER values
COG functional categorization of genes with >1.5-fold ER change
sgRNA design: BLASTN exclusion of multi-aligned candidates; in-house Python script selecting first match per 100-nt window

RNA-seq: CLC Genomics Workbench mapping to NC_000913.3 (length/similarity 0.9); DESeq2 normalization; DEGs = >2.0-fold change and Padj < 0.001; iModulon projection of log2 expression (LB-centered) onto P1K iModulon structure via pymodulon
ChIP-Seq: CLC mapping (0.9/0.9); MACS2 peak calling with default settings; peaks in ≥2 replicates = binding events; DOOR2.0 operon annotation
Knockout growth comparison: Welch's t-test, significance threshold P < 0.1 (as printed in FIG 4C caption)
FlowJo v10.2 for flow-cytometry analysis
analysis_methods.notes: Welch's t-test threshold of P < 0.1 is reported verbatim from the FIG 4C caption and not corrected.

value: Initial library contained 39,574 of 39,591 designed sgRNAs (99.96% coverage)

Under gentamicin, ERs decreased for many ribosomal protein genes, ribosome-associated proteins (e.g., rbfA 5.0-fold, yqjD 4.7-fold) and rRNA-modifying enzymes (e.g., rsmD 4.1-fold, rlmB 4.0-fold), indicating increased essentiality

Toxin-antitoxin systems (ghoST, relBE, yafNO, mazEF, higBA) showed >2-fold ER reductions; antitoxin knockdowns (e.g., ghoS 9.8-fold, relB 7.0-fold) caused stronger fitness defects than toxin knockdowns; no polar effects observed

OMP/assembly genes showed decreased ER (ompA 3.8-fold, bamE 2.6-fold, nlpE 1.8-fold) except bhsA, which showed the highest ER increase (reverse fold change 3.8); multiple efflux pump genes (tolC, acrA, mdtB/E, macA/B, emrK, mdtI, mdtK, etc.) showed 1.5–2.6-fold ER decreases

Gene-level fitness changes under gentamicin strongly correlated with anaerobic conditions (Pearson r = 0.93); E. coli was completely resistant to gentamicin anaerobically (Fig. S2, supplement unavailable)
Knockdown of riboflavin/quinone/heme cofactor biosynthesis genes increased ER under both gentamicin and anaerobic conditions (e.g., fre 67.0-/73.8-fold; ubiD 30.4-/45.6-fold; hemX 4.7-/6.6-fold)
KEIO deletions Δfre, ΔubiX, ΔubiC, ΔhemX were less sensitive to gentamicin than wild type; ΔbhsA conferred complete gentamicin resistance (FIG 4C)
ΔarcA, ΔarcB and ΔcpxR significantly increased gentamicin sensitivity; ΔcpxA had little effect (FIG 5B)

CpxR bound 933 genomic positions under gentamicin vs 51 anaerobic and 13 in LB; 929 of 2,348 gentamicin-induced DEGs were directly associated with CpxR binding; CpxR bound regulatory regions of nuo, cyo, cyd respiratory complexes and arcA
CpxR mediated repression of nuo/cyo/cyd respiratory systems and collapse of membrane potential under gentamicin; the collapse was absent in BW25113ΔcpxR (FIG 6C)
outcomes.notes: Outcomes are direct observations as reported in Results and figure captions. Mechanistic statements (e.g., CpxR limiting gentamicin influx via membrane depolarization) are author interpretations, recorded as claims in experimental_design_object, not as verified causality. Per-gene ER values depend on Table S3 (unavailable).

source_locations.section: Abstract
source_locations.quote: We employed CRISPR interference screening to investigate the fitness efect of each gene in Escherichia coli exposed to gentamicin, aiming to understand the cellular defense mechanisms.

source_locations.section: Introduction
source_locations.quote: Using a high-resolution CRISPRi library, we identified gentamicin-sensitive genes on a genome-wide scale and explored their roles in resistance.

source_locations.section: Introduction
source_locations.quote: Understanding the lack of function in anaerobic environments may shed light on the mechanisms underlying antibiotic resistance. Therefore, we also examined the fitness changes of E. coli under anaerobic conditions to gain further insight into resistance mechanisms against gentamicin.

source_locations.quote: cells were analyzed with an S3e Cell Sorter (Bio-Rad) using a 488 nm laser.

source_locations.section: Materials and Methods: Chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP) sequencing
source_locations.quote: Library quality was assessed using a TapeStation 4150 (Agilent, CA, USA) with a high-sensitivity D1000 ScreenTape (Agilent).

source_locations.section: Results: Genome-wide gene fitness analysis using CRISPRi library screening
source_locations.quote: The enrichment ratio (ER) for each gene was defined as the median of the normalized sgRNA ratios across the positions targeted in the gene.

source_locations.section: Results: Similar fitness changes in anaerobiosis and gentamicin treatment
source_locations.quote: Pearson correlation coeficient (r) analysis revealed a strong correlation between the ER ratio of genes under anaerobic conditions and gentamicin treatment (r = 0.93)

source_locations.section: Materials and Methods: RNA sequencing (RNA-Seq) and analysis
source_locations.quote: Genes with more than a 2.0-fold change in expression and a Padj value <0.001 were considered diferentially expressed genes (DEG).

source_locations.section: Materials and Methods: Chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP) sequencing
source_locations.quote: Binding peaks were identified using MACS2 software with default settings (72).

source_locations.section: Results: Genome-wide gene fitness analysis using CRISPRi library screening
source_locations.quote: We confirmed that the initial library included 39,574 sgRNAs, representing 99.96% coverage (Table S1).

source_locations.section: Results: Fitness changes of toxin-antitoxin systems in response to gentamicin
source_locations.quote: While ghoT showed a 1.5-fold decrease in ER under gentamicin, ghoS showed a dramatic 9.8-fold decrease

source_locations.section: Results: Similar fitness changes in anaerobiosis and gentamicin treatment
source_locations.quote: Deletion of bhsA, encoding a stress-resistant outer membrane protein that increases hydrophobicity (44), conferred complete gentamicin resistance (Fig. 4C).

source_locations.section: Results: Regulation of respiratory complexes by CpxR and ArcA
source_locations.quote: Deletion of arcA, arcB, or cpxR significantly increased sensitivity to gentamicin, whereas cpxA deletion had little efect (Fig. 5B).

source_locations.section: Results: Regulation of respiratory complexes by CpxR and ArcA
source_locations.quote: Under gentamicin, CpxR bound to 933 positions in the genome, compared to just 51 under anaerobic conditions and 13 in LB control (Table S7).

source_locations.section: Results: Regulation of respiratory complexes by CpxR and ArcA
source_locations.quote: Flow cytometry analysis revealed that CpxR mediated the collapse of membrane potential in response to gentamicin, as this collapse was absent in the cpxR knockout strain (Fig. 6C).

stages: EXP1: in silico sgRNA design → oligo synthesis → Gibson assembly → Endura transformation → plasmid pool → QC amplicon sequencing
EXP2: library into MG1655+pdCas9 → pooled culture (LB / LB+Gm / anaerobic) → harvest → amplicon NGS → ER analysis
EXP3: RNA-seq (triplicate, 3 conditions) → DESeq2 → iModulon projection
EXP4: KEIO knockout growth validation under gentamicin
EXP6: DiOC2 flow cytometry membrane potential (BW25113 vs ΔcpxR)
experiment_workflow.design_then_verify_note: Library design choices (EXP1) precede screening (EXP2); knockout, ChIP and membrane-potential experiments are downstream validation/measurement stages, not new engineering designs.

ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: Authors actively designed and constructed a high-resolution sgRNA library tiling all CDS at 100-bp intervals (Q1: explicit design action; Q2: implemented in this study; Q3: an active design choice among library-design alternatives, not a measurement).

design_action.description: Designed 39,591-sgRNA genome-scale library targeting NGG PAMs every 100 bp across all E. coli MG1655 CDS; synthesized as oligo pool; cloned via extension PCR + Gibson/NEBuilder HiFi into pgRNA-bacteria backbone.

ddr_annotations.design_action_rationale: Stated before the action: 'CRISPRi eficiency can vary depending on the genomic structure or interactions between the dCas9 complex and DNA... To overcome this, we designed a high-resolution genome-scale CRISPRi library' (genome_wide_gene_fitness_analysis_using_crispri_library_screening_p001).
ddr_annotations.trigger_observation: Known position-dependent variability of CRISPRi efficiency and difficulty of ensuring consistent efficiency across environmental conditions (author-asserted, no citation at that sentence).
ddr_annotations.evidence_grading_rationale: evidence_basis_type=author_assertion for the variability rationale; the resulting library's 99.96% coverage is experimental_measurement but does not comparatively test the tiling choice against alternatives.
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: Rationale invokes a mechanism (position-dependent dCas9-DNA interaction efficiency) stated prior to the design; however it is asserted without citation, so confidence in the mechanism attribution is moderate.
alternatives_considered: Conventional designs targeting a single or a few positions per gene (mentioned as existing practice the authors chose to exceed); no explicit comparison experiment performed.

ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: Selection of sub-lethal gentamicin concentration 1 µg/mL for the screen (Q1: explicit condition-design choice; Q2: chosen in this study; Q3: design parameter selection, not a readout).

design_action.description: Used gentamicin at sub-lethal 1 µg/mL for screening, RNA-seq, knockout growth, ChIP-Seq and membrane-potential assays.

ddr_annotations.design_action_rationale: Chosen based on the authors' dose-response curve (Fig. S1) and literature reporting that this concentration induces resistance and stress responses including biofilm formation (ref 17).
ddr_annotations.trigger_observation: Dose-response curve of MG1655 library under gentamicin (Fig. S1; supplement not provided) — temporally prior to the screen.
ddr_annotations.evidence_grading_rationale: evidence_basis_type=experimental_measurement (own dose-response) but the underlying data are in the unavailable supplement, plus literature_precedent (ref 17); cannot be independently checked here.
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: Concentration derived from the authors' own dose-response measurement prior to screening; literature citation is supportive context.

ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: BLASTN-based exclusion of multi-aligned sgRNA candidates (Q1: explicit design-filtering action; Q2: done in this study; Q3: design choice affecting library composition).

design_action.description: Excluded multiple-aligned sgRNAs from candidates via BLASTN analysis against the reference genome to avoid off-target binding.

ddr_annotations.design_action_rationale: Stated in Methods: exclusion was performed 'to avoid of-target binding'.
ddr_annotations.trigger_observation: Anticipated off-target binding of multi-mapping sgRNAs (design-stage consideration, stated before construction).
ddr_annotations.evidence_grading_rationale: evidence_basis_type=author_assertion/computational_prediction (sequence alignment); off-target rates were not experimentally measured in this paper.
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: Rationale is the mechanism that multi-mapping spacers cause off-target repression; stated as design motivation, not separately validated here.

ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: Fixing the nucleotide upstream of each spacer to 'A' (Q1: explicit sequence-design choice; Q2: done in this study; Q3: design decision about library sequence context).

design_action.description: Set the nucleotide upstream of the 20-nt spacer sequence to 'A' in every oligo.

ddr_annotations.design_action_rationale: Stated: 'To minimize the deviation in transcription activity due to the transcription start nucleotide.'
ddr_annotations.trigger_observation: Anticipated transcription-start-nucleotide-dependent variability in sgRNA transcription (design-stage consideration).
ddr_annotations.evidence_grading_rationale: evidence_basis_type=author_assertion; no citation and no comparative test of alternative nucleotides in this paper.
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: Mechanistic claim about transcription initiation nucleotide effects, author-asserted without citation; kept as mechanistic_inference with low evidentiary weight.

ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: Construction of chromosomal C-terminal c-myc-tagged CpxR in MG1655 (Q1: genome-engineering action; Q2: performed by the authors in this study; Q3: design choice to enable CpxR immunoprecipitation; decisionhood is measurement-enabling but involves an engineered construct).

design_action.description: Added a c-myc tag to the C-terminus of chromosomal cpxR in E. coli K-12 MG1655 for ChIP-Seq.

ddr_annotations.design_action_rationale: Stated purpose: 'For ChIP-Seq'; tagging method adopted from ref 65 (PCR-based tandem epitope tagging).
ddr_annotations.trigger_observation: Need to map genome-wide CpxR binding under gentamicin after iModulon analysis implicated CpxR (EXP3/EXP5 logic order as presented in Results).
ddr_annotations.evidence_grading_rationale: evidence_basis_type=literature_precedent for the tagging method (ref 65); tag functionality for CpxR not independently validated in this paper.
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: Method explicitly adopted 'as previously described (65)'; rationale is precedent-based rather than mechanistic.

conflicts.conflict_reason: Methods names the library-construction host as Endura competent cells, whereas the Results narrative and FIG 1 caption name E. coli DH5α for the same initial plasmid library transformation step; these are not identical strain identities and cannot be reconciled from the available text.
conflicts.review_action: Check the original published PDF/supplement or contact authors; do not silently prefer one source. Until resolved, treat the library-construction host identity as contested; downstream genotype reconstruction is unaffected (host used only for plasmid propagation without dCas9).

candidate_values: bhsA: 3.8-fold ER increase under gentamicin (reverse fold change 3.8)
conflicts.conflict_reason: The identical magnitude 3.8 is reported for two different genes with opposite ER directions in the same figure context; both may be correct, but the coincidence cannot be verified without the figure visual or Table S3, and a transcription error cannot be excluded.
conflicts.review_action: Verify against FIG 2C source data / Table S3 (supplement) before using either value quantitatively.
